sources.title: Bounded variations and read-only original measurement check
Vocabulary and document count identities
sources.details: Current tiny demonstration: actual 277=256+21 with target 280. Original saved experiment: 512=8+256+248. Original 192 families: floor(.8*192)=153; floor(.9*192)=172; validation=172-153=19; test=192-172=20. Counts exact, bytes measured on encoded original UTF-8, not characters or tokens.

claims.statement: Only observed characters can miss unseen names/characters; ByteLevel with the complete 256-byte alphabet gives unseen valid UTF-8 text a fine-grained representation.
claims.scope: Exact rules used here: full ByteLevel alphabet, no normalizer, no prefix-space addition, no truncation. Coverage is not the distinct BPE byte_fallback option or a guarantee for arbitrary generated IDs.

evidence.supports: UTF-8 bytes map injectively to 256 internal symbols before BPE.
Unseen symbols supplied by initial_alphabet are kept without the optional alphabet limit.
Every represented base symbol can be tokenized before learned merges; without vocabulary coverage absent characters are not reconstructed automatically.

claims.statement: The shown Tokenizer/BPE/ByteLevel/BpeTrainer calls train segmentation rules on two strings, encode to Encoding.tokens and Encoding.ids, and ByteLevel decode plus assert recover 小鳥🙂new.
claims.scope: All APIs in the original fence are covered as one runnable tokenizer configuration; it fits a tokenizer, not neural language-model weights. print and assert only display/check its output.

evidence.supports: models.BPE() selects BPE model rules.
ByteLevel(add_prefix_space=False) and ByteLevel.alphabet() arguments used here.
vocab_size, initial_alphabet and show_progress trainer settings.
decoders.ByteLevel() configures the inverse byte decoder.
String input, list training corpus, encode/decode return contracts and defaults.
The displayed tokens and IDs are corresponding string/numeric views of the same encoding.
Unmodified original fence was executed successfully, not inferred from syntax.

verification.expected: Exact restored string 小鳥🙂new; assertion succeeds on CPU
verification.observed: exit 0; restored string exact; no helper guard events
verification.details: The one original fence was run without changing trainer, decoder or input.

claims.statement: 280 is a target vocabulary budget, leaving a small merge budget beyond 256 base symbols; a small corpus can stop below this target. Special, base and merge entries all take vocabulary IDs.
claims.scope: The tiny original fence defines no special tokens. It obtains 277=256+21, which the text allows; 280 is not a universal guaranteed output size or general hard bound below mandatory starting entries.

evidence.supports: Specials and initial alphabet are allocated first; empty pair queue or insufficient frequency can stop merging before the target.
Exact cardinality arithmetic and independent smaller-data variation.

verification.expected: Complete 256 symbols; <=280 on this specified configuration; tiny corpus may stop before target
verification.observed: Original actual277,21merges; one-char corpus actual256 with target280
verification.details: Current tokenizer JSON and vocabulary are counted; original demonstration has added_tokens=[].

claims.statement: Odd visible token spellings are byte aliases, and whole-sequence ByteLevel decode preserves the original unseen text, including the 未見字🦊 exercise and whitespace/newline variants with the same rules.
claims.scope: Complete encoding of valid Unicode text, not token-by-token readable characters or arbitrary partial/generated byte strings. Individual tokens may split a code point.

evidence.supports: Visible aliases are converted to bytes and concatenated before UTF-8 conversion; a single token need not be valid Unicode alone.
Seven short independent variations pass exact equality.

verification.observed: 7/7 exact roundtrips, including combining marks, NUL and non-BMP/max-scalar cases
verification.details: These variants hold the trainer/decoder/normalizer configuration fixed; UTF-8 hex is saved for exact comparisons.

claims.statement: Saving and pairing the exact tokenizer/ID definitions matters: refitting a same-size vocabulary can assign different pieces to existing IDs and cannot be blindly substituted in an old model.
claims.scope: A possibility under different learned rules/corpora, not a claim that identical data deterministically must change ID meanings. Model pairing needs serialized rules/hash, beyond vocabulary cardinality.

evidence.locator: add_special_tokens 295–307; merges new_token_id 539–549 and model assignment 607–624
evidence.supports: Vocabulary IDs are assigned to corpus-derived merged strings.
Saved JSON represents the serialized tokenizer configuration.
Input ID indexes embedding rows and predicts corresponding output categories.
Original repository checks vocabulary/type/hash/special bindings rather than guessing a matching size.

claims.statement: The original fixed-package experiment selected 96 stories and 96 poems, split complete documents first, then took <=256-byte UTF-8-safe prefixes; BPE trained only on 153 train prefixes, leaving 19 validation and 20 test documents unused for merges.
claims.scope: Read-only audit of the original run and its original data/code hashes; no new data preparation or tokenizer/model training. Exact-content family split does not assert all near-duplicates are absent.

evidence.supports: Selection, complete-document split, safe prefix and train-only iterator are explicit in source matching the original run's code hash.
Family-level seeded allocation produces 153/19/20 before prefix conversion.
Local original assets/splits/hash and every one of 192 row/prefix identities were independently checked.

verification.observed: All192 rows matched; train31970,validation3894,test4193 raw UTF8 bytes; maxima256bytes; split file hashes exact
verification.details: Original raw asset hashes matched result assets; current candidates matched result data hashes; independent computation checked each prefix against its original complete document.

claims.statement: The saved original tokenizer has 512 entries including eight boundary markers, and the reported 未見字🦊 new and whitespace/newline strings restore exactly.
claims.scope: Original serialized tokenizer ec08c61… and original roundtrip records are verified under current tokenizers0.23.2; the original result omits its tokenizers package version. This verifies saved-rule compatibility, not identical refitting across unknown versions or language comprehension.

claims.statement: Practical vocabulary decisions need unseen-text lengths and model costs; roundtrip is a property of the complete tokenizer configuration and is not evidence that a language model understands meaning.
claims.scope: No model-quality, equal-FLOP or universal vocabulary recommendation is asserted in6.3. Linked long training recipes were inspected as contracts only. Same document exposure in the later experiment does not fix tokens/parameters/FLOPs.

evidence.supports: Tokenizer normalization/preprocessing/model rules jointly determine representation, and training invokes the BPE trainer rather than neural-language-model optimization.
Prefix-space configuration can change original text; inverse decoder works on the resulting byte sequence.
Learned tokenizer rules use frequency counts, not language-model semantic training.
Later comparison explicitly declares equal raw-document schedule while token/parameter budgets differ.

factual_accuracy.details: Eight substantive claim groups independently checked; training, encoding, full alphabet, inverse decode, ID binding and original evidence agree with manuscript.
